in_greek.name: Γάβ
in_greek.long_meaning: Γάβ (Gav) προέρχεται από την ελληνική και σημαίνει 'το θρέμμα' .  Η ονομασία Γάβ έχει τις ρίζες του στην αρχαία ελληνική γλώσσα.  Στη Βίβλο, το όνομα Γάβ (Gav) εμφανίζεται ως προσωνύμιο για τον Θεό.  Η ονομασία Γάβ έχει σχέση με την ιδιότητα του Θεού ως θρέφτη και φύλακας των ανθρώπων.  Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα Γάβ συμβολίζει την προστασία και την φροντίδα του Θεού για τα παιδιά του.

in_english.name: Gav
in_english.long_meaning: Gav is a name of Hebrew origin, meaning 'to lift or to exalt'.  In the Bible, the name Gav appears as a title for God, signifying His power and authority.  In Christian tradition, the name Gav symbolizes God's protection and care for His children.  Gav is also a shortened form of names beginning with the letters Gav, such as Gabriel, which means 'God is my strength'.  The name Gav is associated with qualities such as strength, courage, and faith.  In modern times, the name Gav has become popular in some Christian cultures, particularly in the United States.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Gav" has a rich cultural history, particularly for the Jewish community. It is rooted in the Hebrew language, which has been an integral part of Jewish culture for thousands of years. The name has been borne by notable figures in Jewish history, including the Israelite warrior Gideon and the priest Eleazar, who played significant roles in the Old Testament. These biblical characters underscore the meaning of the name - 'God is my strength' or 'God is the source of my power'. The name "Gav" thus evokes a sense of courage, determination, and unwavering faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The Hebrew meaning of the name "Gav" - 'God is my strength' or 'God is the source of my power' - holds great spiritual significance. It is a reminder that, no matter the challenges or trials that life may bring, God is always there to provide us with the strength and power we need to overcome them. It is a name that inspires faith, trust, and reliance on God, and serves as a constant reminder of the power and presence of the Divine in our lives.
